title: 1961 AHSME Problem 38
statement: Triangle \(ABC\) is inscribed in a semicircle of radius \(r\) so that its base \(AB\) coincides with diameter \(AB.\) Point \(C\) does not coincide with either \(A\) or \(B.\) Let \(s=AC+BC.\) Then, for all permissible positions of \(C:\)

solutions.text:
By Thales’ theorem, \(ABC\) is right at \(C.\) Put \(p=AC\) and \(q=BC.\) Then \[ p^2+q^2=AB^2=4r^2. \] Since \((p-q)^2\ge0,\) we have \(2pq\le p^2+q^2.\) Therefore \[ s^2=(p+q)^2\le2(p^2+q^2)=8r^2. \]

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: The angle subtended by the diameter is a right angle
If the legs are \(p\) and \(q,\) compare \((p+q)^2\) with \(2(p^2+q^2)\)
